boundary_timing.note: Same routed netlists with an assumed 1ns external input/output max delay, 0.1ns min. Includes input membrane range monitor timing. No board measurement or reroute.

notes: Beta231 changes saved model dynamics; no retraining
Every neuron is counted; incomplete groups padded with zero
Complete-group cycle formula is for the tested MP1, one-group-at-a-time interface, without intergroup overlap
Total-update proxy adds one cycle per paired active input and one threshold/reset cycle for each six-neuron block; these are not full-neuron RTL timing results

range_certificates.note: Inductive bounds for beta231, arbitrary allowed binary patterns, paired current prefixes, and one hard or subtractive reset per timestep. Not a universal bound for other coefficients.

notes: Implemented interface transfers all six int11 values atomically, with a register bank and no intergroup overlap
Serialized read/write costs are analytic scenarios, not synthesized memory wrappers
Ideal overlap ceiling assumes enough buffers and perfectly overlapped independent reads/writes; controller and buffer costs omitted
At two values/clock, both three-lane and two-lane issue pipelines need at least three memory clocks per six-neuron group

fixed_three_algebra.note: Three full-range operations are algebraically possible in a fixed DSP format; larger high correction cost is not simulated/routed here. Two lanes per DSP is not an absolute packing-capacity bound.

next_shared_offset_screen.formula: Choose b=-16 for an int5 triple, else b=32*(U0//32) when all three upper parts agree. U=b+r, 0<=r<32; pack three delta*r products; exact floor correction uses one shared delta*b/256 quotient and a4-bit carry per lane.
limitations: Arithmetic and opportunity screen only; no RTL, area, timing or overhead for the offset controller
Three full-range fixed residue packing with per-lane high corrections remains a necessary comparison
Correlated synthetic bursts have identical lanes in early phases; the larger stress opportunity is not evidence of natural-model burst acceleration
More eligible groups do not establish a net latency/resource gain

notes: Arithmetic schedule audit only: zero-pair skipping and metadata/output bypass logic have not been built or routed
Uses the existing MP1 service formula: one clock for a zero group, otherwise active issues plus three pipeline/service clocks
Models have128 hidden and10 output neurons; six-lane groups contain padded zeros, including complete zero pairs
The tested adaptive RTL does not skip individual zero pairs; both tested fixed and adaptive cores skip only all-zero groups
The optimistic adaptive schedule additionally skips zero triples and selects the cheaper eligible two/three format; it is not tested RTL

limitations: Leakage-only unit; synaptic accumulation and threshold/reset are software in model replay
Six int11 values transferred atomically to/from a register bank; no implemented BRAM/DRAM operand interface
No intergroup overlap; interface/scheduler/pipeline/state costs included for this unit
Individual zero pairs and padded tail pairs are not skipped by the tested RTL; a stronger zero-pair baseline is screened analytically only
Shared delta in [0,31]; per-neuron coefficient regrouping is not implemented
Beta231 changes saved model dynamics; no retraining, and no equivalence claim to the models at their original beta
Actual RTL model replay covers first48 held-out images per seed; whole360-image profiles are numerical
Boundary timing assumes 1ns max and0.1ns min external delays; OOC port segments remain partially unrouted, so boundary paths are estimates, not timing closure
Fabric FF counts exclude DSP/BRAM internal registers; no power, host-speed or FireFly implementation comparison
Fixed three-wide residue packing is arithmetic-only, not routed; two lanes is not an absolute full-range packing bound
